gloss: to look through, to skim, to glance over

definitions.gloss: to look through, to skim, to glance over
definitions.explanation: To read or review something quickly to get the general content without reading every detail.

examples.japanese: {報告書|ほうこくしょ}に{目|め}を{通|とお}しておいてください。
{契約書|けいやくしょ}には{必|かなら}ず{目|め}を{通|とお}すべきだ。
examples.english: You should always look through contracts.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}、{新聞|しんぶん}に{目|め}を{通|とお}す。
examples.english: I skim the newspaper in the morning.

examples.japanese: {資料|しりょう}にざっと{目|め}を{通|とお}した。
examples.english: I quickly glanced through the materials.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {目|め} (eye) + を + {通|とお}す (to pass through). Literally 'to pass one's eyes through' something.

NUANCE: Implies quick review rather than careful, thorough reading. Often used for:
- Documents, reports, contracts
- Newspapers, magazines
- Email, messages

DEGREES OF THOROUGHNESS:
- {目|め}を{通|とお}す: skim, look over (quick)
- ざっと{目|め}を{通|とお}す: very quick glance
- しっかり{目|め}を{通|とお}す: look through carefully

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {読|よ}む (to read) - general, neutral
- {熟読|じゅくどく}する (to read thoroughly) - careful reading
- {斜|なな}め{読|よ}み (skimming) - reading diagonally
- {一読|いちどく}する (to read once through)

OTHER {目|め} EXPRESSIONS:
- {目|め}が{離|はな}せない: can't take eyes off
- {目|め}を{配|くば}る: to keep an eye on
- {目|め}を{引|ひ}く: to catch one's eye
